properties.areaDesc: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 22 at 3:29AM PST until November 22 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 1.75 to
2.00 feet above ground level is possible along shorelines and
low-lying coastal areas of Grays Harbor County. Inundation
along the northern coast may be around 2.30 to 2.60 feet above
ground level.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County
Coast zones.

* WHEN...From 7 AM this morning to 3 PM PST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is
expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of
parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road
closures expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Increasing waves along the Pacific coast
may also increase water levels around high tide Sunday morning.
While impacts may be limited on Sunday, additional rounds of
coastal flooding will be expected during additional high tides
early next week.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

properties.description:
Areas of fog will impact portions of Southeast Georgia through
mid-morning. The fog could become locally dense at time with
visibilities dropping to 1/4 mile or less. The nature of the fog is
such that visibilities will vary greatly over short distances with
the risk for locally dense fog being the greatest near bodies of
water and other low-lying areas such as marshes, swamps and large
ditches. Motorists should remain alert for these conditions this
morning.

Some locations that will be impacted by the fog include Reidsville,
Glennville, Ludowici, Darien, Hinesville, Claxton, Metter, Portal,
Statesboro and Pembroke.
properties.instruction:
If driving, slow down and leave extra distance ahead of you in case a
sudden stop is needed.

properties.areaDesc: South Central Oregon Coast; Curry County Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 22 at 1:34AM PST until November 25 at 11:00AM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...Coastal areas of both Curry and Coos counties.

* WHEN...From Monday morning through Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Roads may be closed including parts of Highway 101
near the ocean. Low lying property including homes,
businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated.
Some shoreline erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest risk of coastal flooding will
be associated with the high tides in the morning hours.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Inland Colleton; Dorchester; Inland Berkeley; Coastal Colleton; Charleston; Tidal Berkeley
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 22 at 4:34AM EST by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
Areas of fog will impact much of Colleton, Charleston, Berkeley and
Dorchester Counties through mid-morning. The fog could become locally
dense at time with visibilities dropping to 1/4 mile or less. The
nature of the fog is such that visibilities will vary greatly over
short distances with the risk for locally dense fog being the
greatest near bodies of water and other low-lying areas such as
marshes, swamps and large ditches. Motorists should remain alert for
these conditions this morning.
properties.instruction:
If driving, slow down and leave extra distance ahead of you in case a
sudden stop is needed.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 22 at 4:30AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
Areas of fog will continue across parts of southeast Georgia and
northeast Florida through the early morning hours. Patchy dense
fog is expected which will reduce visibilities to less than 1/2
mile on roadways at times. Fog should then dissipate by mid
morning, by 10 AM. It is possible fog could become dense over
more locations which would require a dense fog advisory.

The nature of the fog is such that visibilities will vary greatly
over short distances. If driving this morning, slow down, use
low-beam headlights and leave extra distance between you and the
vehicle in front of you.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued November 22 at 1:21AM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
ESFSEW

A series of progressive systems will bring rain to western Washington
starting Tuesday and continuing into the weekend. The heaviest
rainfall is expected late Wednesday into Thursday, with rainfall
amounts over the Olympics ranging generally between 2 to 3 inches.
This will lead to rises on the Skokomish River in Mason County late
Wednesday into Thursday. Flooding will be possible starting midweek
and continuing into the weekend.

Please monitor the latest river forecasts from the National Weather
Service for additional information.

travelers should allow for extra time and be prepared for changing
conditions.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding
expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, coastal flooding
possible.

* WHERE...North and Central Coast of Oregon, and South
Washington Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4
AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Monday
night through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Major flooding, up to two feet above ground level,
during high tides is possible along the immediate coast as well
as low lying areas near bays, sloughs, and the lower reaches of
the coastal rivers.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal
overflow flooding of low-lying areas is expected due to high
tides. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert for
rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

A Coastal Flood Watch means that more significant coastal
flooding due to a combination of high surf and high tides is
possible. Coastal residents should be alert for later statements
or warnings, and take action to protect property.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that conditions favorable for
flooding are expected to develop. Coastal residents should be
alert for later statements or warnings, and take action to
protect property.

properties.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory, IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 AM
EST THIS MORNING.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors
closed as much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

preparations for rising water and take appropriate action to
protect life and property.

Astronomical Tide or HAT.

properties.areaDesc: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 21 at 7:06PM PST until November 25 at 3:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal
flooding possible. Most susceptible time of flooding will be
around the time of the morning high tides between about 730 AM
and 930 AM.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM Monday to 3
AM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of
sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas,
especially around the time of high tide, including over
beaches, roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is
possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highest risk likely Wednesday and
Thursday with potential for significant impacts. Elevated to
high surf is expected much of the week, peaking on Wednesday
and Thursday. Additional products will likely be needed into
Friday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

properties.areaDesc: Marion
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 21 at 10:05PM EST by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
The officials at the Office of Sustainability for the City of
Indianapolis have called for a Knozone Action Day, IN EFFECT UNTIL
10 AM EST SUNDAY.

A Knozone Action day means that a combination of high temperatures,
light winds, and other factors are expected to produce conditions
where high levels of ozone emissions may exceed federally mandated
standards.

Fine particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Here are some recommended actions that the public can take:

* Walk, bike, carpool or use public transportation.
* Avoid using the drive-through and combine errands into one trip.
* Avoid refueling your vehicle or using gasoline-powered lawn
equipment until after 7pm.
* Turn off your engine when idling for more than 30 seconds.
* Conserve energy by turning off lights or setting the air
conditioner to 75 degrees or above.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 21 at 6:54PM PST until November 26 at 1:00PM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal
flooding possible.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4
AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST
Tuesday through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the
increase next week, exceeding 7 feet by Sunday. Highest tides
will be Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily
high tides each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach
7.9-8.2 feet, likely re-breaking the all time tidal records
set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides
will remain around 3- 5 feet through Wednesday, but an
incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably
higher surf beginning on Thursday. Uncertainty remains in
exact surf heights at this time, but look to be 6-8 feet with
sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 21 at 8:36PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has maintained a steady climb through Moderate Flood
Stage on the St Johns River at Deland, with river levels forecast to
reach Major Flood Stage late this weekend. A steady rise through
Major Flood Stage is anticipated through next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 5.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Saturday was 5.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise into Major Flood Stage
early next week, reaching 6.0 feet mid week. Additional rises are
possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday afternoon at noon EST.

- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Saturday was 4.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to gradually rise through Major
Flood Stage, reaching 4.3 feet into the middle of next week.
Additional rises thereafter will be possible.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday afternoon at noon EST.

mph possible.

Weed, Gazelle, Grenada and Montague.

especially for high profile vehicles.

to tough driving conditions given the strong southerly wind speeds.

profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

inflatable holiday decorations that could be blown around or damaged
by the wind.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 21 at 2:30PM PST until November 26 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 2.8 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Pacific Ocean Coast.

* WHEN...Through 4 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.0 ft above normal (7.8 ft MLLW)
at 8:48 AM Sunday, 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 9:25
AM Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM
Tuesday, 2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM
Wednesday, and 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM
Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 21 at 2:45AM EST until November 22 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and rough surf.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...Through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 315 PM MST Friday Nov 27.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 313 PM MST, a streamflow gauge has indicated that water from
an upstream dam release from Painted Rock Dam has reached
Dateland. Flooding is expected along the Gila River within the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.areaDesc: Elkhart
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued November 20 at 10:31AM EST by NWS Northern Indiana
properties.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory for Elkhart County, in
effect from 6 PM Saturday November 21st to 10 AM EST Sunday November
22nd.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors closed as
much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/
